summary: M4.3b LeaseManager, final binding round. FIRST, the no-Java-change claim is MEASURED, not taken on trust: I extracted the `diff --git a/sequencer/...` section from the round-4 packet (declared sha256 26e846ae...) and from this one (a7446a99...) and they are byte-identical, sha256 8df2008228325c9b82cc9a477640abea6f227dd6776cadddbbe4d55b68b5383d on both -- all 748 lines covering LeaseManager.java, LeaseManagerTest.java and StatBlindStore.java. The ONLY delta between the two staged diffs is docs/internal/product/backlog.md: the M4.12 hunk is gone entirely (`git show HEAD:...` and `git show :...` of the M4.12 row are identical, so that row is back to its committed text), the M4.3b row gained a corrected owner sentence, and three rows were added. So my round-4 production and cost verdict stands unchanged and I did not re-litigate it: acquire = stat+putIfAbsent (cold) or stat+get+putIfMatch (takeover) or stat+get (refused), renew = exactly one putIfMatch with no re-read, release = one or zero. All O(1) per node per term or per renew interval; no LIST; a non-holder renew returns before touching the store. Request rate scales with nodes and time, never with records, shards, partitions or indices -- non-negotiable 6 holds. R4-2 VERIFIED FIXED and the fix is honest. The false clause is gone from M4.12 (grep for `synchronized` in the staged backlog returns only M4.3b's design sentence and M4.3c). M4.3c's three factual claims each check out: (a) `round-3 test review measured that removing synchronized from all four sites leaves the whole suite green` matches .harness/review/a62849c5....test-reviewer.json verbatim ('MEASURED. Replacing all four occurrences of public synchronized with public leaves all 29 tests green'); (b) ingest/src/test/java/binjava/ingest/StoreFakes.java:32 GatedCommit does hold putIfAbsent open on two CountDownLatches over a delegate, at T1, so the parked justification really was false and the row says so in those words rather than quietly dropping it; (c) `synchronized` really is on four sites (held, tryAcquire, renew, release). The proposed mechanism also works, which is the part that matters if this row is not to be another parking space: gating stat() lets thread B enter the read-decide-CAS window while A is blocked, and because adopt() nulls held/heldVersion on a lost CAS, the loser can be observed clearing the winner's belief -- a positive assertion, not a timing one. R4-3 VERIFIED FIXED: M4.10's row is `Commit idempotency on (podId, flushSeq) with lastAppliedFlushSeq per pod | FR-3`, confirming it never touches the lease CAS, and both the new M4.3d row and the corrected sentence in M4.3b now say the earlier attribution was wrong instead of silently re-pointing it. M4.3d's consequence trace matches the code: renew() catches nothing, so an ambiguous putIfMatch leaves held/heldVersion at their pre-PUT values, the node keeps sequencing a term it genuinely still holds (safety holds, epoch preserved by renewedUntil), and ADR-0007 lines 44-46 do put ~10 s TTL-expiry failover inside what is accepted. One nuance about the tightened number is finding R5-1. R4-1 VERIFIED RECORDED as M4.3e, with the constraint I asked for stated explicitly ('NOT a blanket clear ... conditional on holderPodId and epoch'), and recording rather than fixing is the RIGHT call here: the fix is a behaviour change needing its own red record in a commit already at round five, `grep -rn LeaseManager --include=*.java` outside src/test finds only Lease.java's javadoc, so there is no production caller at all -- blast radius is zero as the row says -- and review.md rule 11 is explicit that fixing a minor is usually wrong because the next round's surface is the prose the fix just added. OWNERSHIP, the pattern being broken: all three rows are now self-owned. Nothing is parked on a task that cannot carry it, and each row names the specific mechanism that would close it (a gated store, an ADR-or-version-refresh, a conditional clear). IDs: `grep -oE '^\| M[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[a-z]? '` over the staged backlog yields no duplicates; M4.3c/M4.3d/M4.3e are new and unused elsewhere; every ID the new prose cites resolves (M4.1, M4.10, M4.12, M4.8, ADR-0007, FR-11, NFR-9 all present). The letter-suffix convention matches M4.3b/M1.1b/M1.15d, and sdd.md rules 2 and 4 are satisfied. Two things I looked at and decided are NOT findings: the M4 SPEC's task table does not list M4.3c/d/e, but that table says in its own second line 'One commit each, decomposed in backlog.md', and the M0.53 precedent puts review-derived debt in the backlog only; and the M4.3b row does not point forward to M4.3c or M4.3e the way it now points to M4.3d, which is a cosmetic asymmetry given both rows sit directly beneath it and name M4.3b's own code. One minor, non-blocking.

findings.title: M4.3d's 'TTL-minus-renewInterval' is tighter than the code guarantees and disagrees with M4.3b's own sentence in the same commit
findings.failure_scenario: M4.3d says the cluster has no sequencer 'for up to TTL-minus-renewInterval'; the M4.3b row four lines above says 'for up to a full TTL'. Both describe the same failure and only one can be the bound. The tighter figure -- which originated in MY round-4 finding, so this is my error being faithfully transcribed -- holds only if the holder's next renew comes exactly one renewInterval after the ambiguous one. LeaseManager.renew() lets the IOException escape and leaves held/heldVersion untouched, so the retry policy is entirely the caller's, and 'the store was unreachable' is precisely the error a caller retries IMMEDIATELY. Concretely: the PUT lands at T extending expiry to T+TTL, the response is lost, the caller retries renew at T+epsilon, that CAS loses against the version its own landed write created, the node concludes it is fenced and stops sequencing at T+epsilon, and nobody can take over until T+TTL -- a gap of nearly a FULL TTL, not TTL minus renewInterval. Nothing is unsafe and it stays inside ADR-0007's accepted TTL-expiry failover either way, which is why this is minor and why the verdict is unaffected; but a future reader deciding between 'accept in an ADR' and 'carry a version-refresh' will weigh a number that is up to renewInterval too small, and M4.3b's looser 'up to a full TTL' is the one that is actually true. The honest form is 'up to a full TTL; TTL-minus-renewInterval when renew is driven on a fixed interval rather than retried on the ambiguous error'.
